name: Aragorn, King of Gondor
oracle_text:
Vigilance, lifelink
When Aragorn enters, you become the monarch.
Whenever Aragorn attacks, up to one target creature can't block this turn. If you're the monarch, creatures can't block this turn.
blocked_sentences: When Aragorn enters, you become the monarch.
Whenever Aragorn attacks, up to one target creature can't block this turn. If you're the monarch, creatures can't block this turn.

needs.what: The monarch designation as game state: at most one player is the monarch at a time, that player draws a card at the beginning of their end step, and a player becomes the monarch whenever a creature they control deals combat damage to the monarch. Needs the designation stored on GameState (a player id or None), the two automatic behaviours above wired into the end step and the combat damage step, and a `condition_keys` entry (e.g. `is_monarch`, taking a player selector) so "If you're the monarch" can be asked by an `if` op.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `set_flag`/`has_flag` is the nearest thing and only stores an opaque per-card boolean: it is not exclusive across players, nothing moves it when a creature deals combat damage to its holder, and no end-step draw hangs off it, so a card written on flags would say "you become the monarch" and deliver none of what monarch means. `docs/rules-coverage.md` records the monarch as not implemented; nothing in `src/` matches /monarch/.

needs.what: An op that makes a player the monarch -- `become_monarch` with a player selector ("you", "target opponent", "each player in turn order" is not needed) -- setting the designation above and firing whatever triggers watch it change.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: No op in `ops` grants a designation. `set_flag` is the closest and writes a card-scoped flag with no game-wide meaning; there is no monarch state for any op to set until the engine need above lands.

needs.what: A one-shot op that imposes "can't block" on chosen creatures for the rest of the turn -- `objects` for the targeted form ("up to one target creature can't block this turn") and a way to say it of every creature on the battlefield for the global form ("creatures can't block this turn", which must also catch creatures that enter later in the turn, so it is a turn-scoped continuous effect and not a per-object mark).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cant_block` exists only as a `static_effects` entry: it lives in an ability on a permanent, is read by `characteristics.block_forbidden` off `_battlefield_statics`, lasts exactly as long as its source is on the battlefield, and its `affects` filter may read only printed characteristics -- so it cannot name a creature chosen when a trigger resolves and cannot expire at cleanup. `detain` is the only op that stops blocking and is wrong twice over: it also forbids attacking and activating abilities, and it lasts until the detainer's next turn rather than this turn. `grant_ability` cannot carry the static instead -- `loader.py` explicitly rejects any grantable ability that is not triggered, because a granted static would have to enter the characteristics pipeline from a non-source object. `block_restriction` points the other way (it restricts who may block a given attacker) and `must_block` is a requirement, not a restriction.
